title: Sealed classes and exhaustive when
context: What is a sealed class, and why does it help with `when` expressions?

refs.title: Atomic Kotlin (book) by Bruce Eckel & Svetlana Isakova

answer: A sealed class restricts which classes may extend it. Its direct subclasses must be declared in the same package and module (since Kotlin 1.5). Because the set of subclasses is known, a `when` expression over a sealed type can be exhaustive without an else branch. If you later add a subclass, the compiler reports every `when` that is no longer complete. Use sealed types to model a closed set of results, such as success or failure outcomes.

points.title: Closed hierarchy
points.why: The compiler knows every subclass, so it can check completeness.

points.title: Exhaustive when
points.why: A complete when over a sealed type needs no else, and adding a subclass breaks the build where it is missing.
